q: For QAOA MAX-CUT under depolarizing noise, at what two-qubit error rate p2* does the p=2 approximation ratio stop dominating p=1, as a function of graph regularity, girth, and max-cut degeneracy?
basis: In our single 3-regular n=10 seed, r_{p=2} > r_{p=1} for p2 <= 1e-2, ties at p2=3e-2 (0.729 vs 0.724), and flips to r_{p=2} < r_{p=1} at p2=1e-1 (0.620 vs 0.659). We saw the crossover exists but have no statistics on its position across graph families.
next_steps: Repeat the p1/p2 sweep on an ensemble of 100+ 3-regular graphs at n=10, 12, 14; add 4-regular and Erdős-Rényi ensembles; fit p2*(graph_stats) with logistic regression to expose the geometric drivers.

q: How much of the observed <1% ratio degradation at NISQ noise (p2=1e-3) is preserved when QAOA parameters are re-optimized under the noise model versus using the noiseless optimum, and does noise-aware training buy measurable extra robustness only in the p2 > 1e-2 tail?
basis: Preskill emphasizes that variational hybrid re-optimization is the mechanism by which NISQ circuits absorb noise. We only evaluated the noiseless optimum under noise; the delta between noise-aware and noise-naive optimization was not measured.
next_steps: For each p2 in the sweep, re-run COBYLA with the noisy expectation as the objective (Aer-shots gradient-free), report r_noisy_re-opt vs r_noisy_from-ideal, and check whether the gain scales linearly with p2.

q: Depolarizing noise is a worst-case symmetric channel; how does the same QAOA circuit degrade under matched-total-error but temporally correlated 1/f dephasing that better approximates superconducting-qubit low-frequency noise?
basis: Preskill's 'gate error ~1e-3' is a scalar; our numeric sweep instantiates it as Markovian depolarizing. Correlated dephasing accumulates coherently across the 60 CX gates in p=2 and could produce a very different sensitivity curve.
next_steps: Use pyGSTi or Qiskit's ThermalRelaxationError with T2*/T2 asymmetry and a coherent Z-drift channel matched to total infidelity 1e-3, then compare r(p2) curves.

q: Does the shape of the noise-sensitivity curve r(p2) at n=10 survive scaling to n=20-25, or does concentration of measure at larger n flatten the curve entirely (a symptom of barren-plateau-like behaviour)?
basis: Preskill's thesis is a claim at 50-100 qubits, but our experiment is at n=10 where classical brute force is trivial. Any statement about NISQ 'at scale' is extrapolation from this instance.
next_steps: Rerun for n in {12, 16, 20, 24}, use MPS or GPU statevector where needed, and log both r(p2) and the variance of the QAOA gradient at random parameters as an early barren-plateau indicator.

q: Our AerSimulator has no hardware connectivity; a real IBM heavy-hex or Sycamore compile of this 3-regular n=10 graph would inflate CX count 2-4x via SWAP overhead. How much of the observed graceful degradation disappears once realistic SWAP inflation is included at fixed per-gate noise?
basis: Our p=2 circuit had 60 CX assuming all-to-all connectivity; on a physical NISQ device the effective depth is much higher and the argument 'graceful under NISQ noise' has to be re-tested at the compiled depth, not the algorithmic depth.
next_steps: Transpile with qiskit-ibm-runtime FakeSherbrooke (heavy-hex) and Cirq's Sycamore layout, re-run the noise sweep at the compiled CX count, and report r_compiled/r_algorithmic as a function of p2.
